interest: FBI and State Department intelligence on wartime Japanese communism, including Nosaka's Yan'an manifesto.
overview: State Department decimal file 894.00B (Japan: Bolshevism, Communism, Communistic Activities, Subversive Activities) covers documents spanning October 1940 through September 1944 relating to Communist and subversive activities in wartime Japan. The file predominantly comprises personal and confidential intelligence communications from FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr., with information shared with military and naval intelligence. Topics include a detailed 1944 report on Japanese Communist Party leader Susumu Okano's (Sanzo Nosaka) escape to the Chinese Communist Eighth Route Army and his analysis of deteriorating Japanese domestic conditions, a 1941 report on suspected Communist machinery sabotage at the Kanebo Spinning Mills in Osaka, a 1943 report evaluating Soviet intelligence penetration in Japan via Communist underground channels, and internal State Department cross-reference sheets concerning alleged German fifth column activities behind the 1940 arrests of British subjects in Japan.

subfiles.about: Cover letter from FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover transmitting a confidential intelligence memorandum on Communism in Japan to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr.
subfiles.summary: Hoover sends Berle an intelligence memorandum on Communism in Japan, copied to Naval Intelligence and G-2, 1944.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Adolf A. Berle, Jr. Transmitting Memorandum on Communism in Japan

subfiles.about: Intelligence memorandum on Japanese Communist Party leader Shushumu Okano (Sanzo Nosaka) reaching Chinese Communist headquarters and issuing a revolutionary program for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Japanese Communist leader Shushumu Okano (Sanzo Nosaka) reached Yan'an and declared Japan's defeat by the United Nations a short cut to a people's government. He urged underground organizing and cited Japan's economic exhaustion and falling morale.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Communism in Japan and Program of Shushumu Okano

subfiles.about: Intelligence letter reporting suspected Communist sabotage that damaged machinery and caused a temporary shutdown of the Kanebo Spinning Mills in Osaka.
subfiles.summary: Hoover tells Berle that suspected Communist sabotage halted the Kanebo mill in Osaka for a week after June 10, 1941, with many arrests.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Adolf A. Berle, Jr. Regarding Sabotage at Kanebo Spinning Mills

subfiles.about: Intelligence letter reporting that the Soviet Union obtains inside intelligence on Japan through an efficient Japanese Communist Party underground network.
subfiles.summary: Hoover tells Berle that Russia has the best inside information on Japan through the underground Japanese Communist Party.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Adolf A. Berle, Jr. on Soviet Intelligence and the Japanese Communist Party

subfiles.about: Internal Department of State charge slip documenting the charging of file 894.00B/62 to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip for document 894.00B/62, sent to FE on June 19, 1942.
subfiles.title: Charge Slip for File 894.00B Document 62

subfiles.about: Division of Far Eastern Affairs cross-reference sheet summarizing a newspaper report on German fifth column activities leading to the arrest of British subjects in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Coville's cross-reference to a 1940 Shanghai Evening Post claim that Germany instigated arrests of British subjects in Japan.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Cross-Reference Sheet on German 'Fifth Column' Activities in Japan
